sections.heading: The Prayer of Thanksgiving
sections.body: *Translated by Samuel Zinner; edited by Mark Mattison (Other Gospels Nag Hammadi Initiative)*

sections.heading: 1. Gratitude for Revelation
sections.body:
**1.** “To you we give thanks!

**2.** To you is every soul and heart lifted up,
 O tranquil name, honored with the name ‘God,’
 and praised with the name ‘Father.’

**3.** For to everyone and everything is the fatherly compassion and tenderness and love,
 and every possible instruction that is sweet and clear,
 imparting to us mind, speech, knowledge.

**4.** Mind: that we would understand you.
 Speech: that we would explain you.
 Knowledge: that we would know you.

**5.** We rejoice, enlightened by your knowledge.

**6.** We rejoice, because you have revealed yourself to us.

**7.** We rejoice, because when we were in the body
 by your knowledge you made us divine.

sections.heading: 2. To Know the Father
sections.body:
**1.** The thanksgiving of the one who reaches you is this one fact:
 that we know you.

**2.** We have known you, O light of the intellect.

**3.** Life of life, we have known you.

**4.** Womb of every created being,
 we have known you.

**5.** The pregnant womb bearing the essence of the Father,
 we have known you.

**6.** Eternal continuance of the Father who begets,
 in this way we have worshiped your goodness.

**7.** One favor we ask:
 we wish to be preserved in knowledge.

**8.** And one shelter we desire:
 that we stumble not in this manner of life.”

Having said these things in prayer, they embraced one other, and they departed to eat their holy, bloodless food.
